scope.area: Signature event operating suite and reusable global event journeys
requirements: Real Signature Productions Giannis Ploutarchos and Andromache concert March 20 2027 at Parkview Manor: source-faithful room/table explorer, original poster and floor plan, physical venue tour, responsive guest planning and organizer operations. Printed 100–275 prices confirmed per guest; currency/tax/fees remain unconfigured.

Front stage sponsor lounges: two facing white five-seat benches with a central table, approximately ten people. Side stage lounges: open rectangular white seating around a central area, approximately twenty-five or more. Do not assign these descriptions to numbered inventory without organizer confirmation.

Organizer imports and edits price lists, photographs, menu sections, bottle packages, modifiers, allergens, explicit taxes/service charges/currency, stock, service zones, last-order cutoffs and age/staff checks. Preview before publish; version conflicts and rollback; no inferred free prices or stock.

Guest ordering from verified table context routes bottles/drinks to assigned servers and bar queues with accepted/preparing/ready/delivered/rejected states, staff override audit, sold-out recovery, duplicate-request protection and reconnect reconciliation.

Full bill splitting before and during event: ticket shares, own items, equal/custom amounts, shared bottle allocations, discounts, taxes, service charge, optional tips, paid/refunded balances, cash staff receipts, outstanding shares and late orders. Exact money conservation and concurrent payment reservation; no client-paid status.

Temporary inventory holds with expiry, atomic table/seat confirmation and payment reconciliation. Distinguish source-plan preferences, private saved plans, enquiries, held inventory and actual tickets; no fabricated available seats.

Subtle disclosed actionable sponsorship on table details, bottle/menu context and event screens: active scoped organizer-approved placements, frequency caps, offer expiry, redemption authorization, accessible touch alternative to hover, no automatic popups covering seat or checkout controls.

Event social sharing: shareable public event cards and deep links, opt-in guest photo/video submissions and hashtags, organizer moderation, content rights and people permission, revocation/removal, screen-safe projection, expiry, reporting, event-scoped media retention and authorized provider ingestion. Hashtag alone is not public-screen consent.

Drag and drop for authorized organizer table layouts, sponsor placements and menu order, and guest-owned group/itinerary/shared-item organization. Keyboard/buttons alternative, touch support, undo, stale versions, permission checks; guests cannot change inventory or other groups.

Scoped messaging: guest-to-organizer questions, private invited-group planning, table-to-assigned-server assistance, order-linked issues, staff handoff, block/report, mute, rate limits, attachment checks, participant revocation, delivery receipts and no cross-tenant or cross-table leakage.

Owner setup/readiness dashboard connects actual business ownership, venue, inventory, catalog, staff routing, taxes, policies, merchant account and moderation team before activating operational features. No payment information entered for the current sales showcase.

Web, iOS and Android journey parity assessed explicitly; native deep links, upload/camera, QR scan, notification permission, offline/foreground recovery and accessible interactions. Responsive web alone is not native delivery.

Acceptance includes simultaneous last-seat/last-bottle requests, expired holds, double clicks, uncertain responses, stale quotes, payment/webhook duplication, voids/refunds, staff turnover, venue/table transfer, social-content takedown during display and inaccessible provider embeds.

client_ecosystem_delivery.central_requirement: Every entity is an individual client; a generic directory card is not completion.

sections.area: Preserve And Execute The Whole Vision
requirements: Read applicable repository instructions, current specifications, prior product decisions, unfinished work and docs/recovery-scope.json.
Recover every previously requested capability. Do not silently drop requirements because George gives another example or identifies another defect.

Maintain one complete capability and acceptance matrix covering client homes, enrichment, websites, community, Studio, AI, marketing, SEO, analytics, communications, commerce, events, sector tools and native mobile.
Existing code is a starting point—not the specification or the quality standard.
Reuse sound infrastructure. Redesign, consolidate or replace inadequate implementations. Preserve data, ownership, consent, valid links and audit history.
Coordinate product, design, engineering and independent QA responsibilities with clear ownership. Do not repeatedly ask George to identify missing professional requirements.

sections.area: Make Every Incoming Lead Start A Real Client Workflow
requirements: Implement an automatic, durable workflow:

Lead received → identity resolved → official sources verified → website researched and crawled → offering understood → structured content and media prepared → individual experience composed → operational tools connected → quality reviewed → published according to existing authority and review rules → kept current.
Persist real progress, timestamps, evidence, errors and next actions.
Resolve duplicates and branches before creating another entity. Match exact business/person identity, location, domain and relevant ownership context.
A successful HTTP request, completed scraping job or AI-generated paragraph does not mean enrichment is complete.

If a source cannot be accessed, preserve the lead, identify precisely what is unavailable, retry appropriately and use permitted alternative sources. Never silently substitute generic content or report success.
Make the pipeline resumable and bounded. One difficult website must not stop unrelated leads.

sections.area: Crawl The Website To Understand The Client
requirements: Do not stop at the homepage, metadata or first image.

Discover and inspect relevant navigation, sitemaps and linked pages, including:
- About, history and team.
- Services, specialties and service areas.
- Menus, products, prices, packages and offers.
- Booking, ordering, shopping and enquiry paths.
- Locations, hours, accessibility and contact information.
- Events, classes, programs, performances and calendars.
- Galleries, portfolios, media, videos and downloads.
- FAQs, policies and relevant customer information.
- Verified social and external provider links.
Process relevant PDFs and structured data. Use rendered-page extraction where necessary for accessible JavaScript content.
Use deterministic extraction where reliable and AI where interpretation is needed. Do not spend AI calls on work ordinary parsers can perform correctly.
Normalize and validate phone numbers, email addresses, URLs, dates, timezones, currencies, units and location information.
Separate permanent offerings from expired promotions, historical events and outdated prices.
Distinguish company headquarters, operating branches, service areas and worldwide activity.
Respect source access restrictions and usage rights. Do not bypass logins or invent inaccessible information.
Protect crawling infrastructure against malicious URLs, private-network access, excessive downloads and runaway recursion.

sections.area: Create An Individual Client Brief Before Composing The Home
requirements: For each entity, derive a structured brief from evidence:

Who is this client?
What do they actually offer?
Who are their customers or members?
What makes them different?
What should a visitor understand immediately?
What are the most valuable customer actions?
What visual identity do they use?
What content and imagery are available?
What operational tools do they need?
Which actions can Zoi fulfill directly?
Which depend on an external provider?
What remains unknown?
The brief must influence the actual rendered experience.
A category label is only the beginning. Two restaurants, two barbers or two churches can require substantially different presentation and workflows.
Do not invent differentiators, credentials, prices, testimonials, awards, facilities or services.
Preserve the distinction between an independently sourced, unclaimed presence and an owner-managed home. Never imply that the client commissioned, endorsed or controls an unclaimed page.

sections.area: Design Each Home As An Individual Client Project
requirements: Build the experience around that client’s identity, strongest assets, offering and customer priorities.

Determine appropriate:
- Page structure and content hierarchy.
- Hero composition and image treatment.
- Typography and colour direction.
- Navigation and section order.
- Service/product presentation.
- Galleries, storytelling and supporting media.
- Calls to action.
- Relevant trust information.
- Mobile interactions.
- Booking, purchase, contact and participation journeys.
Use the client’s visually verified logo and real photographs. Preserve correct aspect ratios and identity. Do not mistake a partner logo, stock image or unrelated photograph for the client.
Do not transplant another client’s content or imagery.
Improve weak source presentation while preserving factual accuracy. An outdated source website should not force Zoi to reproduce its design problems.
Use high-resolution originals where available, intentional crops, responsive derivatives, readable overlays and appropriate image attribution.
Avoid generic AI filler, identical section order, repeated marketing slogans, irrelevant modules and empty decorative space.
Shared engineering is expected. Shared generic presentation is not.

Build reusable components and composition rules capable of different layouts, content priorities and sector workflows. Do not create hundreds of fragile copied codebases or one universal page with different names.
Preserve owner-selectable designs and editing capabilities. Owner edits and explicit removals must override imported or generated defaults.

sections.area: Implement Sector-Specific Customer And Owner Journeys
requirements: A barber’s home should reflect the actual barbershop: services, prices, team, styles, portfolio, location, hours and booking or walk-in arrangements where evidenced.
A restaurant’s home should express its actual atmosphere and offering: food photography, menus, prices, dietary information, hours, reservations, ordering, catering or private events where offered.
A creator or artist needs relevant media, releases, channels, performances, collaborations, booking and audience relationships.
A professional needs accurate services, qualifications, specialties, languages, service areas, intake and appropriate private client workflows.
A church or community organization needs its actual identity, leadership, announcements, published schedules, programs, volunteering, membership and supported giving.
Schools, cultural groups, sports clubs, event organizers, retailers, hotels and property providers need their own operational logic.
Do not attach a generic appointment calendar to accommodation inventory or label an enquiry as a confirmed reservation.
Only display actions supported by the client’s offering and actual connected workflow. Complete the required integrations rather than leaving decorative controls.
Preserve all previously requested sector scope, including recipes, dance groups, festivals, sports leagues, coordinated events, travel/property discovery and company administration.

sections.area: Connect Every Client Home To Its Operating Workspace
requirements: The public home and owner tools must manage the same canonical information.

Owners should be able to:
Claim and verify ownership → review imported content → correct it → manage their brand → preview → publish → operate their offering → measure results.
Editable fields must cover real business content: menus, products, services, pricing, hours, staff, events, images, policies and calls to action.
Provide team permissions, version history, private drafts, approvals, conflict handling and rollback.
Test edit → preview → publish → public API → rendered web/mobile output.
Do not maintain a beautiful public page that the owner cannot actually manage.
Do not create competing profile editors, content stores, calendars or contact databases.

sections.area: Make Enrichment Continuous And Owner-Safe
requirements: Keep provenance for important fields and assets: source URL, retrieval time, extracted evidence, transformation and verification state.

Trace problems across:
Source → extraction → stored record → API projection → rendering → customer action.
Detect missing API projection fields as well as missing extraction.
Monitor meaningful source changes without repeatedly reprocessing everything. Distinguish a proposed update from an approved owner change.
Do not overwrite owner edits, resurrect explicitly removed content or publish uncertain changes silently.
Provide review queues for identity conflicts, questionable imagery, contradictory prices, expired information and blocked sources.
Measure coverage across the entire affected catalogue. A handful of curated examples does not prove that the pipeline works for everyone.

sections.area: Build The Shared Zoi Foundation Properly
requirements: Use one canonical account and explicit personal, creator and organization contexts.
Share identity, ownership, permissions, brand knowledge, assets, content, campaigns, contacts, consent, conversations, events, products, bookings, transactions and analytics.
Define authoritative systems, stable IDs, synchronization rules and conflict resolution.
Web and native apps must consume consistent business contracts.
Use durable jobs for crawling, media processing, AI, publishing, synchronization and notifications.
Implement validation, authorization, idempotency, bounded retries, cancellation, progress, recovery and auditability.
Distinguish requested, processing, completed, published, delivered, failed and uncertain outcomes.
Protect tenant boundaries across databases, APIs, storage, caches, background jobs and external integrations.

sections.area: Deliver The Complete Everyday Toolset
requirements:
Recover and cover the existing benchmark scope:
Hootsuite, Buffer, Later, Metricool, Sprout Social, Brand24, Manychat, Canva, Adobe Express, CapCut, Descript, OpusClip, Riverside, Runway, ElevenLabs, Jasper, Linktree, Beacons, HubSpot, Kit, Mailchimp, Semrush, Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity, Shopify, Gumroad, Patreon, Calendly, Typeform, Zapier and Ownr.co.
Use these as capability benchmarks and potential integrations. Build a coherent Zoi product rather than thirty-one disconnected tools.
Research current official provider capabilities, API access, licensing, account requirements and costs.
Decide deliberately what Zoi owns, what uses a specialist provider and what connects to the client’s existing account.
Every tool must have real inputs, execution, persisted outputs, confirmed results, failure handling and a useful downstream workflow.
A link, embed, successful login or attractive screen does not establish functional integration.

sections.area: Make Ai Understand Each Client
requirements: Each workspace’s AI must use that client’s verified offering, brand, content, approved documents, assets and authorized business data.
Generic industry advice is insufficient when client-specific information exists.

The assistant should create useful drafts and perform authorized tasks: campaigns, content variants, website improvements, customer-response drafts, product descriptions, event promotion and performance explanations.
Outputs must remain editable and tied to their source context.
Do not fabricate business facts, available stock, bookings, metrics or completed actions.
Enforce permissions, spending limits and approval requirements. Defend against malicious instructions in crawled websites and uploaded documents.
Evaluate Greek/English accuracy, factual grounding, brand consistency, tool use and recovery.
Record real AI usage and costs. Manual edits must not trigger unnecessary generation charges.

sections.area: Build One Connected Creative And Marketing Studio
requirements: Create branded posts, carousels, reels, videos, stories, posters, menus, event promotions, media kits and website content from each client’s actual identity and offering.
Support editable templates/layers, cropping, resizing, subtitles, captions, thumbnails, video editing, transcription, clipping, revisions and export.
Connect Canva and selected media providers through supported workflows. Return edited/exported assets to the correct Zoi campaign and media library.
Preserve originals, rights and derivative relationships. Provide real upload/processing progress and recovery.
Use one calendar and approval flow for Zoi-native and supported external publishing.
Generate destination-appropriate variants, verify account permissions and confirm actual publication using provider results.
Integrate CRM, forms, segments, email campaigns, sequences and shared inbox workflows. Preserve consent, suppression and unsubscribe state.
A client should move from idea to content to approved distribution without re-entering the same information across tools.

sections.area: Give Each Client Website, Seo And Ai-Discovery Tools
requirements: Inspect both the Zoi home and the client’s own authorized website.

Provide:
Scan → evidence-backed findings → prioritized recommendations → proposed corrections → preview → approval → application → rescan → measurement.
Cover crawlability, indexing controls, metadata, structured data, broken links, mobile usability, page speed, accessibility, content gaps and local information.
Connect authorized search, analytics and business-listing data.
Include AEO/GEO-related visibility work through accurate, accessible, well-structured content. Do not invent scores or guarantee indexing, rankings or AI citations.
Recommendations must reflect the specific client, page, audience and offering—not a generic checklist pasted into every account.
Show the affected URL, actual evidence, severity, confidence, proposed correction and verification result.
Apply changes directly to Zoi-managed content through revisions and approval. Use authorized integrations for external websites; otherwise provide precise implementation instructions.

sections.area: Make Metrics Accurate And Actionable
requirements: Define sources, formulas, periods, timezones and freshness for every metric.
Distinguish zero, unavailable, unsupported and delayed data.
Connect discovery, content, enquiries, subscribers, bookings, sales and retention without misrepresenting attribution.
Provide client-specific explanations and next actions. A restaurant, creator and parish do not need identical dashboards.
Measure whether changes improve customer outcomes. Do not claim that a prettier page or higher impression count proves commercial success.
Keep sensitive information out of analytics and recordings. Respect user consent and access permissions.

sections.area: Build Zoi’S Own Community Network
requirements:
Deliver a distinctive network with familiar, reliable capabilities:
Text posts, images, carousels, reels, longer videos, stories, comments/replies, reactions, following, saves, sharing, search, notifications and appropriate private/group conversations.
Use real media infrastructure: resumable uploads, safe processing, thumbnails, transcoding, adaptive playback where appropriate, captions, storage/CDN delivery and deletion.
Test slow networks, interruption, app backgrounding and device resource use.
Build moderation, reporting, blocking, appeals, spam controls, impersonation protection, rights handling and appropriate protections for younger users.
Do not fabricate activity or populate the network with unauthorized copied media.

Connect community content to the actual client ecosystem:
A food video to a restaurant, recipe or product.
An artist reel to verified performances.
A business post to its real offer or booking.
An organization announcement to a program or event.
Build purposeful Parea groups and useful local/global discovery. Support optional hometown, island, city and diaspora interests without inferring sensitive identity.
Make recommendations explainable and controllable. Keep sponsorship clearly disclosed.

sections.area: Finish Commerce, Events And Real Operations
requirements: Connect the existing BuyGreek architecture with Zoi’s profiles, content and customer journeys.
Verify catalogues, variants, stock, currencies, fees, checkout, orders, fulfillment, refunds, payouts, memberships and digital access.
For events, complete owner setup, publication, real inventory, timed holds, payment/reservation, confirmation, tickets, QR check-in and cancellation.
Preserve the full Signature and other venue requirements. Use each organizer’s actual branding, floor plan, imagery, prices and operational configuration.
Prove concurrency, hold expiry, group allocation, split payments, duplicate webhooks and uncertain-outcome recovery.
An illustrated room is not live inventory. A request is not a confirmed booking. An external checkout link is not a completed purchase.

sections.area: Connect The Platform Through Real Automation
requirements: Use shared triggers, conditions and actions with authorization, consent, logs, limits and recovery.

Prove connected workflows such as:
Client offering → branded campaign → approved website/social/email publication → customer action → operational fulfillment → analytics.
Lead arrival → verified crawl → individualized home → quality review → claim invitation workflow where authorized → owner activation.
Website problem → proposed correction → approval → publication → rescan.
Prevent duplicate sends, feedback loops and runaway provider costs. Revoked access and withdrawn consent must stop affected future actions.
A suggestion is not authorization to send, publish, charge or delete.

sections.area: Deliver Professional Web And Native Experiences
requirements: Preserve Zoi’s approved identity while allowing client homes their own art direction. Zoi should provide coherent navigation and infrastructure without visually flattening every client.
Use readable typography, intentional hierarchy, polished imagery, accessible controls and restrained motion.
Verify complete phone, tablet and desktop journeys. Test light/dark themes, long names, Greek text, large accessibility text, keyboard use and reduced motion.
Use the established native app and account/backend model. Verify actual iPhone, iPad and Android behavior, not only responsive web.
Test authentication, deep links, media, maps, uploads, notifications, bookings, tickets, provider handoffs, durable drafts and account switching.
Keep public, owner and administrator experiences appropriately separated.

sections.area: Apply Per-Client Acceptance And Site-Wide Coverage
requirements:
A client home is complete only when:
- Identity and sources are correct.
- The client’s actual offering is represented.
- Important source content is accounted for.
- Branding and imagery are visually verified.
- Layout and content priorities suit that client.
- Customer actions lead to real outcomes.
- Owner controls manage the published content.
- Web and mobile are usable.
- Permissions and privacy hold.
- Remaining unknowns are explicit.
- Evidence is recorded.
Use a rubric with objective requirements and independent visual judgment.
Check representative populated, sparse and difficult records in every affected family, plus automated coverage across the catalogue.
Do not claim all-client completion from a sample. Identify precisely which records passed, failed or remain unverified.
If a page looks like the same generic template with a different name, investigate whether the client brief actually influenced its composition.

sections.area: Harden, Verify And Release The Whole Product
requirements: Run meaningful unit, integration, browser, database, provider and native-device tests.
Exercise real journeys and failure paths, including wrong users, wrong tenants, revoked access, stale revisions, duplicate requests, concurrency, timeouts and provider rejection.
Verify encryption, least privilege, secure secrets, safe mobile storage, audit trails, backup retention and an isolated restore.
Review dependency vulnerabilities, uploads, injection, account recovery, webhooks, crawler security and private-data exposure.
Instrument crashes, errors, latency, database load, queue health, synchronization, delivery and spend. Set measurable operational objectives, alerts and recovery procedures.
Use isolated test data and provider test environments. Do not perform destructive production testing, real bulk outreach or live charges as QA.
Release through reviewed PRs, protected controls, safe migrations and rollback plans. Verify actual production domains and distribute the corrected mobile build through existing authorized channels.
Do not stop at “the code exists,” “the build passed” or “the PR is open.”

sections.area: Handle External Dependencies Without Abandoning The Work
requirements: Verify provider capabilities, production access, scopes, app review, licensing, quotas and account requirements.

For every genuine owner-dependent blocker, give George:
The service, affected workflow, current state, exact setup location, required setting/credential NAME, approval or fee, his precise action and the final verification test.
Never print secrets or ask for them in chat. Do not incur unapproved spending.
Prepare everything possible before requesting the final owner action. Continue all unblocked work.

sections.area: The Definition Of Done
requirements: A business arrives as a lead. Zoi understands its actual website and identity, builds an individually considered home, connects the tools appropriate to its offering, lets the owner manage it, helps it create and distribute content, supports real customer actions and measures the results.
A member encounters compelling people, businesses, culture and content, can participate naturally and has useful reasons to return.
The web and mobile products operate as one ecosystem.
Every advertised tool performs its intended job. Every important workflow has verified success and recovery behavior. Every completion claim has evidence.
